A1.justification: Both PDFs describe S2R-HDR and S2R-Adapter. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, HDR reconstruction comparisons, adaptation experiments and ablations in Tables 1–7 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds further adaptation, video reconstruction, temporal consistency and runtime results.

M1.justification: The adapter architecture, scaling rules and teacher-student updates remain unchanged. Appendix B.7 explicitly extends the rendering pipeline to produce optical flow, depth, diffuse reflectance and surface normals alongside HDR frames, constituting a limited pipeline extension.

E1.justification: v2 adds direct evaluation on Kalantari and adaptation tests on Sen and Tursun datasets. It also introduces HDR video reconstruction using Vimeo-90K, Sintel and Real-HDRV training data, with evaluation on DeepHDRVideo and the TOG HDR dynamic dataset (Appendices A.6–A.8). Kalantari already appeared as a training source in v1.

E2.justification: The original image-fusion comparator networks are retained. v2 introduces HDRFlow-based video comparisons, including Vimeo+Sintel-trained and Real-HDRV-trained baselines against S2R-HDR training (Table 14), and adds a Challenge123-pretrained S2R-Adapter comparison in Table 9.

E3.justification: v2 adds pooled SCT+Challenge123 training and fine-tuning controls, supervised and test-time Kalantari evaluation, MUSIQ scoring for Sen/Tursun, video reconstruction and flow-warping temporal evaluation, and timed adaptation (Tables 4, 8 and 11–17). The original SCT/Challenge123 splits and reconstruction metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original branch, teacher-student and forgetting ablations are retained. New analyses examine pooled real-data training and alternative pretraining (Tables 4, 8–9), temporal consistency (Table 15), motion-direction diversity (Figure 13), and adaptation efficiency (Table 17). The relocated t-SNE and difference-map figures reproduce existing analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both use augmentation variance within the adaptation algorithm; this is unchanged model behavior rather than uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3 and 5–7 retain their values, while v2 adds pooled-data, Kalantari, Sen/Tursun, video, temporal and runtime results. Table 14 newly reports 43.51 PSNR-µ for S2R-HDR pretraining followed by Real-HDRV fine-tuning. v1's Kalantari-trained SCT/Challenge123 results are replaced by different evaluations. Table 9 also reports 43.44 for adapted SAFNet on SCT, conflicting with 43.33 in retained Table 2.

T1.justification: The adapter definitions, rank assumptions and Equations 1–3 are unchanged. v2's Equation 4 supplies the adopted standard flow-warping metric for video evaluation; it introduces no new theoretical result, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about the 24,000-image dataset, two-branch adapter and improved real-world HDR fusion remain. The introduction revises the relative-scale claim from approximately six times existing datasets to 166 times typical datasets and explicitly distinguishes the contribution from GTA-HDR's single-image conversion task.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds explanations for architecture-dependent gains over fine-tuning. Appendix A.12 acknowledges and interprets online adaptation costs, while A.9 and B.7 qualify reproducibility through purchased assets and describe applications beyond HDR as prospective. Earlier texture-domain-gap and knowledge-forgetting interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code/data availability; v2 states public availability and adds a reproducibility statement. It newly documents exposure triplets, approximately 30 supervised adaptation epochs, the rendering workflow, asset and motion provenance, auxiliary outputs, and runtime hardware and image resolution. The epoch and exposure specifications clarify previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against GTA-HDR, discusses SelfHDR and UltraFusion, and adds references supporting video evaluation, quality metrics and test-time adaptation costs. These extend the literature context without substantially redefining the existing synthetic-data and adapter positioning.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the original prose remain. v2 standardizes HDR fusion terminology, clarifies access to ground truth during adaptation, expands explanations, reorganizes appendix subsections, and adds reproducibility, acknowledgement and LLM-use statements. The retained narrative undergoes limited rewriting.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column conference layout, extensively repositioning figures and tables. The dataset t-SNE moves from v1 Figure 2 to appendix Figure 8, Table 1 gains a size column, and new experimental tables and pipeline, motion-direction and auxiliary-output figures substantially expand the displays. Figure 12's caption incorrectly describes optical-flow directions.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens generalization evidence through additional adaptation datasets, video evaluation and controls separating data-source and adaptation effects. Runtime measurements and expanded generation and implementation documentation address important omissions in v1. These gains outweigh localized reporting defects, particularly Table 9's unexplained 43.44 versus 43.33 discrepancy and Figure 12's incorrect caption. The improvement comes from stronger validation and transparency, while the original headline results remain unchanged.
